title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Promotes Diesel Affordability
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Promotes Diesel Affordability The White House October 5, 2026 ADDRESSING AMERICAN DIESEL AFFORDABILITY: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to temporarily allow off-road “dyed” diesel for highway use and defer the applicable Federal excise tax, lowering costs for Americans. The Order directs the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of War, to defer payment of the Federal excise tax imposed for on-road use of dyed diesel fuel for the remainder of the year without interest or penalties, and to explore pathways to eliminate the obligation to pay the deferred taxes. The Order directs the Secretary of Transportation to coordinate with States, industry leadership, and labor organizations on access to dyed diesel. The Order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to ensure farmers’ access to dyed diesel in high-demand areas, and to encourage corresponding action by States. The Order directs the Director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs to encourage more States to adopt policies that correspond with the Secretary of the Treasury’s actions pursuant to this Order. PUTTING MONEY BACK INTO THE POCKETS OF AMERICANS: President Trump is addressing fuel affordability for American consumers, farmers, truckers, and workers. The Administration has already undertaken historic efforts to ensure fuel affordability for Americans, and is taking this action to make available further temporary relief for Americans because of ongoing global conditions affecting the supply of diesel. Farmers and truckers are essential to the American way of life, feeding families, fueling communities, and sustaining the American people. As restricted global diesel supply, driven by the Russia-Ukraine war and a lack of refining capacity around the world, including Democrat-led States that chose to shut down their refineries in the name of “Green Energy” policies, has led to rising prices, further action is necessary to provide Americans with relief. This action will put money directly back in the pockets of American farmers, truckers, and workers, for example saving truckers over $100 per refill. Diesel is taxed based on its intended use. “On-road” or highway diesel is subject to state and federal excise taxes. Diesel used for off-road purposes, such as agricultural, construction, or heating, is not taxed. This off-road diesel is dyed red so that law enforcement can identify it to enforce penalties and back taxes for on-road use. The Administration, and State Governors, can exercise their enforcement discretion to halt inspections and waive the tax liability that users would face for on-road use of dyed diesel. CUTTING COSTS THROUGH AMERICAN ENERGY DOMINANCE AND SUPPORTING AMERICA’S FARMERS AND TRUCKERS: The Trump Administration’s American energy dominance and economic policies are reducing costs and delivering real benefits to hardworking Americans across the country. Since Day One, President Trump and his Administration have fought to rescind the Biden Administration’s inflation-fueling energy regulations, eliminate red tape, and restore America’s position as the world’s leading energy producer. As a result, the United States has reclaimed its position as the world’s leading energy producer and exporter, driving economic growth, lowering costs for families, and bolstering our national security. Under President Trump’s leadership, American energy dominance is back. President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts delivered for America’s farmers and ranchers, putting their hard-earned money back in their pockets. This historic legislation modernized the farm safety net, expanded market access for farmers, and invested in rural economies. Additionally, the Trump Administration has delivered over $40 billion in direct aid to farmers since January 2025. Since President Trump returned to office, the Trump Administration has prioritized American truckers, replacing illegal immigrant truck drivers with American veterans. In that time, American truckers’ earnings have increased by over 7%. The Department of Transportation waived its hours of service rules, allowing truck drivers handling gasoline and diesel shipments to drive additional hours, lowering fuel costs for all Americans. In August 2026, President Trump announced the largest oil deal in world history with Venezuela, securing 65 billion barrels of oil to double America’s oil reserves, increase our oil supply, and lower gas prices for all Americans, long into the future. In October 2026, President Trump successfully negotiated with Europe to release 100 million barrels of refined diesel from its strategic reserves within the next four months. This will increase supply and bring diesel prices down for Americans.

title: President Trump Takes Decisive Action to Lower Diesel Costs for American Truckers, Farmers
text: Releases President Trump Takes Decisive Action to Lower Diesel Costs for American Truckers, Farmers The White House October 5, 2026 Tonight, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to immediately cut diesel costs for the truckers and farmers who keep America moving. The order temporarily opens highway use of tax-free dyed diesel, deferring the federal diesel tax on that fuel through the end of the year — no interest, no penalties. With elevated diesel prices and tightened global supply driven by the Russia-Ukraine war and a lack of refining capacity around the world, this is President Trump’s affordability agenda in action. “Today, I am announcing another unprecedented step to bring down costs. For many years, farm vehicles, construction equipment, and other off-road vehicles have used what is known as ‘red dye’ diesel… which is exactly the same as normal diesel, but is sold tax-free for off-road vehicles and big trucks… Tonight, I am going to sign a historic Executive Order to officially waive the off-road requirement and allow anyone to purchase tax-free red dye diesel for any reason,” President Trump said in Nebraska. The federal diesel tax is 24.4 cents per gallon , or about $60 on a 250-gallon fill. Where states match this federal action, savings will top $100 per fill — a real difference for the hardworking Americans who haul the freight and grow the food. title: President Trump and Republicans Are Delivering Real Results for Nebraska
text: Releases President Trump and Republicans Are Delivering Real Results for Nebraska The White House October 5, 2026 Today, President Donald J. Trump travels to Grand Island, Nebraska. Under President Trump and Republican leadership, families in the Cornhusker State are keeping more of what they earn, farmers and ranchers are getting direct support, private investment is expanding production, and crime is falling in the state’s largest cities. Historic Tax Relief for Nebraskans President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts stopped the largest tax hike in American history and put money back in Nebraskans’ pockets. No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime: Qualified tips and overtime pay are now deductible from federal income taxes, benefiting hundreds of thousands of Nebraska service workers, truckers, manufacturers, and hourly employees. No Tax on Social Security: More than 300,000 Nebraska seniors can benefit from the new deduction that eliminates federal income tax on Social Security benefits for the vast majority of recipients. Bigger refunds: Nebraskans’ average federal tax refund reached $3,378 . Investments in rural health: Nebraska secured nearly $219 million in first-year funding under the Working Families Tax Cuts’ Rural Health Transformation Program — the eighth-largest award in the country — to modernize care in rural communities. Protecting Nebraska’s economy: The Working Families Tax Cuts protected 37,000 Nebraska jobs, preserved $7 billion in state GDP, and safeguarded $3 billion in wages for Nebraskans. Standing with Nebraska Farmers and Ranchers President Trump’s America First agenda is delivering real dollars and new market access to the producers who feed the country. Year-round E15: In April 2025, President Trump’s EPA granted the emergency waiver that cleared summer sales of E15 nationwide, answering the direct request of Nebraska and other Midwestern states and expanding the market for Nebraska ethanol and corn. Direct aid: USDA has delivered $622 million to 36,000 Nebraska Farmers through the Emergency Commodity Assistance Program for the 2024 crop year. Nebraska farmers have also received more than $632 million in Farmer Bridge Assistance payments — part of the $12 billion national bridge program for trade disruptions and higher input costs left by the Biden Administration — with nearly 33,000 Nebraska producers applying. They remain eligible for the $16 billion Supplemental Disaster Relief Program covering 2023 and 2024 crop losses. Ranchers first: In September 2026, President Trump signed two Executive Orders backing American ranchers. One directs action to help producers protect herds from wolves and other predators, and advances country-of-origin labeling transparency. The second orders tougher enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act and expands ranchers’ ability to get cattle to market without compromising food safety. New Investment Across Nebraska President Trump’s economic agenda is delivering major private-sector investment and expansion. Eaton is investing more than $30 million in a new Bellevue facility to expand U.S. production of medium-voltage switchgear for data centers, creating more than 200 new jobs. Becton Dickinson is investing $110 million to expand prefillable syringe production at its Columbus plant, creating about 120 new jobs, on top of its earlier $35 million investment at the same plant. Safer Communities for Nebraskans President Trump’s commitment to law and order is producing real drops in crime in Nebraska’s largest cities. In Omaha, crime is down from last year, including an 11% drop in total crime, a 12% drop in property crime, a 33% drop in criminal homicide, a 21% drop in rape, a 31% drop in robbery, and a 29% drop in auto theft. In Lincoln, violent crime is down 15%, robbery is down 31%, aggravated assault is down 16%, murder is down 75%, and property crime is down 9%. President Trump is in Nebraska to deliver a simple message: promises made, promises kept. Lower taxes, stronger farms and ranches, new manufacturing, and safer streets are the record because Republicans delivered — and Nebraskans cannot afford to hand that progress back.

title: U.S. Leads International Coalition to Endorse Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science
text: Releases U.S. Leads International Coalition to Endorse Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science The White House October 4, 2026 KYOTO, JAPAN — At the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Science and Technology in Society (STS) Forum convened in Kyoto, the United States and 16 countries endorsed the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science . The joint declaration reflects a shared ambition to renew and strengthen our science ecosystems and usher in a golden age of discovery and prosperity. Led by White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, the Kyoto Vision recognizes that we stand at the frontier of an immense opportunity to harness super intelligence and advance new approaches to greatly accelerate scientific discovery. Super intelligence for science will enable autonomous experimentation at scale, unlocking new experimental and analytical capabilities that open entirely new lines of inquiry. In light of the profound shifts in the research landscape, ministers pledged to seize this moment by harnessing new institutional models and funding mechanisms to enable the best and brightest scientists to pursue their most ambitious work. “The way we make scientific discoveries has changed, and the Kyoto Vision is a recognition of that shift and a call to action,” said Director Kratsios. “Super intelligence applied to science will be the greatest force in history for democratizing research. Seizing this moment requires us to reinvigorate our research enterprises and leverage new institutional models for discovery. Under President Trump’s leadership, the United States is leading that charge, and the Kyoto Vision shows the world is ready to move forward with us.” The Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science calls for: Improving the institutions of discovery: Ministers noted the value of a using a variety of funding tools to support research, including long-duration awards, rapid grants, and prizes and challenges, and encouraged experimentation with new institutional models that offer different levels of autonomy, resources, and direction. They welcomed metascience as an empirical field to improve how science is conducted, organized, and funded for public benefit. Harnessing super intelligence for science: Ministers recognized that SI is both accelerating existing research tasks and enabling entirely new forms of inquiry. They encouraged thoughtful integration of SI into scientific workflows and pledged to expand researcher access to SI for science tools, scientific data, computing infrastructure, and experimental facilities. Cultivating talent across the scientific enterprise: Ministers committed to identifying and investing in meritorious students and early-career researchers, and to giving them the support, freedom, and opportunity necessary for ambitious inquiry. They acknowledged that progress in many technological domains depends on people who can operate, maintain, and improve instrumentation, and encouraged expanded hands-on training as well as cross-sectoral doctoral programs, fellowships, and research partnerships. In July 2026, Director Kratsios delivered to President Trump Science: A New Golden Age , the most comprehensive rethinking of the American science and technology research enterprise in eight decades. The report established new directions for U.S. government agencies on how they conduct, fund, and measure the impact of R&D, in light of fundamental changes to the American scientific enterprise and the new opportunities that have emerged. The following countries endorsed the Kyoto Vision for a Golden Age of Science: Argentina Bulgaria Chile Cyprus Germany Greece Indonesia Italy Japan Kazakhstan Republic of Korea New Zealand Poland Singapore United Arab Emirates United Kingdom United States of America

title: NATIONAL MANUFACTURING DAY, 2026
text: Presidential Actions NATIONAL MANUFACTURING DAY, 2026 Proclamations October 2, 2026 BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA A PROCLAMATION For 250 years, American workers have been the driving force behind our Nation’s strength, prosperity, and industrial might. Their skill, ingenuity, and determination have fueled our economy and carried American manufacturing to new heights. On National Manufacturing Day, we honor the men and women who make, build, and create in America — and we celebrate the extraordinary comeback of American manufacturing. As President, my highest priority has been putting America First by restoring our Nation’s manufacturing and bringing back good-paying American jobs. I have imposed powerful tariffs to protect American workers and businesses from unfair trade practices, and as a result, we are seeing the greatest reshoring of American manufacturing in our Nation’s history, alongside a surge in demand for products Made in America. Since I returned to office, I have secured more than $11.2 trillion in United States and foreign investments across manufacturing, critical infrastructure, and technology sectors. Groundbreakings of new factories are surging with 112,000 new factory construction workers building since I returned to office. The factory construction jobs of today mean more good-paying manufacturing jobs for decades to come. These investments fuel job growth, innovation, and opportunity across every corner of our country. I was also proud to sign the Working Families Tax Cuts Act into law — landmark legislation that makes the Small Business Tax Deduction permanent and allows American manufacturers to immediately expense 100 percent of their factory, machinery, equipment, and domestic research and development investments. At the same time, this historic law is putting more money back into the pockets of hardworking Americans and increasing take-home pay, including new provisions like No Tax on Overtime. After declining by nearly $850 under the previous administration, the real wage for the average manufacturing worker has surged by $2,500 annually since I took office. These efforts are driving a revival of American manufacturing and making our country the best place in the world to build, produce, and invest. After years of failed policies that hollowed out our industrial base and left American workers behind, manufacturing is once again powering America’s economic resurgence. After years of decline, manufacturing employment is rising once again with 72,000 new manufacturing jobs added in 2026 so far. Today, we honor the generations of Americans who have built our country through their hard work, and we look proudly to the next generation, who will carry on our great tradition of American innovation and enterprise. Together, we will make American manufacturing bigger, better, and stronger than ever before. NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim October 2, 2026, as National Manufacturing Day. I call upon all Americans to celebrate the entrepreneurs, innovators, and workers in manufacturing who are making our communities strong. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this second day of October, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first. DONALD J. TRUMP

title: Democrats UNANIMOUSLY Vote AGAINST the Stop Insider Trading Act
text: Releases Democrats UNANIMOUSLY Vote AGAINST the Stop Insider Trading Act The White House September 30, 2026 President Trump stands with the American people— no lawmaker, regardless of party or seniority, should utilize insider information for personal profit. In his State of the Union Address to Congress earlier this year, President Trump called for the passage of the Stop Insider Trading Act without delay to ensure that Members of Congress cannot profit from insider information. “As we ensure that all Americans can profit from a rising stock market, let’s also ensure that members of Congress cannot corruptly profit using inside information… Did Nancy Pelosi stand up? Pass the Stop Insider Trading Act without delay. ” – President Trump, State of the Union Address Yet, today EVERY SENATE DEMOCRAT BLOCKED this legislation to root out corruption in Washington and ban Members of Congress, their spouses, and their dependent children from purchasing individual stocks from publicly traded companies. When lawmakers consistently outperform stock trading benchmarks , Americans are rightly asking questions and demanding transparency. title: ICYMI: President Trump Announces Largest-Ever Steel Plant Coming to Iowa
text: Releases ICYMI: President Trump Announces Largest-Ever Steel Plant Coming to Iowa The White House September 30, 2026 President Donald J. Trump announced a $15 billion Mesabi Metallics steel complex is coming to Iowa — the largest steel plant ever built in the United States as more industrial capacity comes home. The project will create 1,750 new, permanent jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and generate an estimated $95 billion in U.S. economic output over construction and the first decade of operations. Iowa leaders are heralding the “transformational” investment: Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds : “I want to thank President Trump for his commitment to bringing steel manufacturing back to America, and Mesabi Metallics for choosing Iowa as its partner and future home. This is a transformational opportunity for our country, our state, and American families—one that strengthens national security, creates thousands of high-paying jobs, and provides a reliable supply of high-quality, American-made steel for strategic goods and everyday products. Our commitment in Iowa to fiscal responsibility, tax competitiveness, and long-term economic stability has created one of the nation’s strongest environments for business investment. Now, this opportunity will fundamentally change the economic trajectory of our state and the entire region for decades to come.” Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird : “This massive investment is the largest steel plant project in U.S. History. It means over 1,750 good-paying, family-supporting, steel working jobs for Southeast Iowa. This announcement is not just good news for Iowa, it’s good for the entire country. Thanks to President Trump for his leadership and continued commitment to American jobs for American citizens and to Governor Reynolds for her hard work bringing this great opportunity to Iowa.” Sen. Chuck Grassley : “GR8 NEWS Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 BILLION steel mill in IA Remember GOP is working 2 bring down costs 4 families + create jobs This historic investment is AMERICA FIRST+builds on success of our Working Families Tax Cuts law which also prevented largest tax increase ever” Sen. Joni Ernst : “Proud to join @POTUS today announcing a historic $15 BILLION investment in eastern Iowa, the largest steel plant in American history, and over 1700 permanent jobs in Iowa! Thank you, President Trump, for bringing jobs, investment, and American manufacturing back home!” Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks : “For too long, Iowa families have watched their jobs shipped overseas and their communities hollowed out. Not anymore. The largest steel plant in America is coming to Lee County with more than 1,700 permanent, good-paying jobs. I’m proud to have helped make this historic investment a reality. There’s no better place than Iowa to make things IN America, BY Americans.” Rep. Ashley Hinson : “This will be a game-changing investment for our state — creating 1,700 jobs & incredible opportunities for growth. There is no better place to invest and build than in Iowa because we have the best people.” Rep. Zach Nunn : “This is a major opportunity for Southeast Iowa: Mesabi Metallics’ proposed $15 billion investment in Lee County could support 1,700 good-paying jobs and produce American steel right here in Iowa. We’ve worked to bring manufacturing home and secured nearly $5 million to strengthen skilled trades training at DMACC, Iowa Western, and Indian Hills. Now, we need to make sure Iowa workers have the skills to be first in line for these jobs and ready to build the next generation of American steel.” Iowa Congressional Delegation : “This historic investment is a major win for Iowa workers and further cements Iowa’s role in the future of American manufacturing. As the largest steel plant investment in U.S. history, this project will generate over 1,700 good-paying Iowa jobs, create new opportunities for Iowa families, and drive economic growth. Iowa has the workforce, work ethic, resources, and business climate to compete with anyone, and we are proud to welcome this project to our state. The administration’s pro-American manufacturing policies are incentivizing companies to invest, build, and create jobs in the U.S. We thank Governor Reynolds for her leadership in making Iowa a great place to do business and ensuring our state benefits from these policies by attracting transformational investments like this one.” Iowa Speaker of the House Pat Grassley : “This project would be a gamechanger for southeast Iowa and leave a lasting impact on our state’s manufacturing footprint. This will bring real jobs that mean stable careers for working families, giving more young people a chance to proudly call Iowa home. I’ve made it my mission in the Iowa House to make sure we bring opportunities for growth to all parts of the state and delivering this plant follows through on that promise.” Iowa Senate Majority Leader Mike Klimesh : “For years, we have been passing legislation to help Iowa grow, draw people to our rural communities, and strengthen our state’s economy. Iowa has an opportunity to bring billions of dollars of investment into our state, good quality jobs, and bring people to a part of Iowa looking for growth. These are the kinds of opportunities we have been looking for and that Iowa needs. As we look to remain competitive on the national level, the largest private investment in Iowa history makes it clear our state is open for business.” Iowa State Rep. Carter Nordman : “$15 BILLION dollar investment in Iowa (largest ever, by far)! Thank you President Donald J. Trump & Governor Kim Reynolds for your leadership on this historic project!” Iowa State Rep. Austin Harris : “HUGE day for Iowa! The President is announcing a $15 billion investment to build America’s largest steel mill right here in our state — more than 1,750 good-paying jobs for Iowa families. This didn’t happen by accident. For years, Iowa has done the hard work of cutting taxes, slashing red tape, and making it cheaper and faster to build here than almost anywhere else in the country. Companies don’t drop $15 billion on a handshake. They go where the rules are clear, the tax climate is competitive, and the workforce can get the job done. That’s Iowa. We made ourselves the place they wanted to be. Now it will pay off in paychecks, apprenticeships, suppliers, and communities that will feel this for a generation. I am proud of this state and proud of the workers who are about to make history. Iowa is open for business! Let’s get to work!” Iowa State Rep. Blaine Watkins : “To have one of the largest steel plants in American history built right here in Lee County would be a huge win for our area. It would mean thousands of high-paying, dependable jobs that would give young Iowans a reason to stay, grow their families, and thrive right here in Southeast Iowa. I’ve been fighting for this kind of opportunity in the Iowa House, and I will fight to get this project over the finish line in the Iowa House.” Iowa State Rep. Matt Rinker : “As a Burlington native, I recognize this announcement for what it is: a once-in-a-generation economic development victory for Iowa. Since being elected to the Iowa House, my priorities have included securing high-paying careers to ensure more people can call Iowa home, and keeping our state competitive in manufacturing apprenticeships and training. The announcement of one of the largest steel plants in American history built right here in Iowa shows that the work we’ve done at the Statehouse, including reducing the tax burden and keeping government spending fiscally responsible is working. In the House, I will fight to deliver this opportunity for my district.” Lee County (IA) Economic Development Group President and CEO Emily Benjamin : “Today is a great day for eastern Iowa. A $15 billion investment with more than 6,000 construction jobs and 1,750 permanent jobs would be transformational for our region, and we congratulate Mesabi Metallics on today’s announcement.” Burlington (IA) Mayor Jon Billups : “What’s great for the southeast Iowa region is great for Burlington and what’s great for Burlington is great for southeast Iowa.” Former Iowa Gov. title: ELIMINATING DISEASE-CARRYING PESTS AND RESTORING ENJOYMENT OF THE GREAT OUTDOORS
text: Presidential Actions ELIMINATING DISEASE-CARRYING PESTS AND RESTORING ENJOYMENT OF THE GREAT OUTDOORS Executive Orders September 29, 2026 Executive Order 14433 By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: Section 1 . Background and Purpose . Ticks and mosquitoes are among the deadliest animals worldwide, transmitting major diseases that impose growing health and economic burdens on the American public. Foreign, invasive mosquitoes, especially the Asian tiger and Egyptian mosquitoes, are multiplying across the United States and have become the dominant species in some areas, including the District of Columbia (D.C.), spreading disease and diminishing quality of life. Furthermore, the expanding tick populations in the United States expose Americans, our pets, and our livestock to debilitating and expensive health risks. Historical approaches have relied primarily on the use of conventional pesticides; however, the use of commonsense, non-chemical, technology-enabled measures can significantly reduce the negative effects of these pests, enhancing enjoyment of the great outdoors for all Americans. Sec . 2 . Policy . It is the policy of the United States to develop and deploy commonsense approaches and technological capabilities to suppress tick and mosquito populations and address the harms these insects cause, using improved detection, screening, prevention, and health care interventions. These goals will be achieved through the following policy priorities: (a) Leading the world in safe and effective tick and mosquito population control to prevent disease through smart land management techniques and procedures, natural predator populations, non-chemical pest control measures, and advanced technologies, including sterile insect techniques and insect control tools developed with safe and effective biotechnologies. (b) Diagnosing, preventing, and treating the syndromes and diseases spread by ticks and mosquitoes in the United States, including alpha-gal syndrome, Theileriosis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Lyme disease, and Babesiosis (spread by ticks), and viral infections such as West Nile, Zika, Chikungunya, and Dengue fever (spread by mosquitoes). (c) Advancing the objectives of the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force set forth in Executive Order 14252 of March 27, 2025 (Making the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful), by reducing the invasive tick and mosquito populations across D.C. both safely and effectively, without negative effects on beneficial insects, native plants and animals, or the natural beauty of our parks, waterways, and recreational areas. (d) Expanding the successful techniques and approaches developed in section 3 of this order as a model for nationwide control of tick and invasive mosquito populations. Sec . 3 . Implementation . (a) Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, and the Administrator of General Services, in consultation with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall develop and implement a campaign across D.C. to, by 2028, reduce the Asian tiger mosquito, Egyptian mosquito, and other invasive mosquito populations, as appropriate, by 90 percent and reduce the tick population by 50 percent, with further reductions as practicable. The campaign shall: (i) remediate tick and mosquito breeding grounds on lands subject to Federal jurisdiction throughout D.C., including by reducing tick and mosquito habitats through landscaping and drainage improvements, e.g., mowing and rain gardens, and strategic deployment of natural, targeted controls; (ii) control pest transport and key host reservoir or amplification populations, including rodents and deer, that facilitate ticks and tickborne diseases; (iii) prioritize the use of commercial capabilities or cooperative agreements, including the deployment of advanced technological solutions such as sterile insect techniques for mosquitoes or other safe and effective biotechnologies; and (iv) include a plan, developed in consultation with the Government of D.C., as appropriate, for implementing tick and mosquito controls on lands across D.C. communities. (b) Within 60 days of the date of this order, to expedite the campaign ordered in subsection 3(a) of this order, the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, in consultation with the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall: (i) submit to the President, through the Assistant to the President and Homeland Security Advisor, a regulatory framework, informed by relevant academic centers and industry, for the planned development and release into the environment of advanced, safe, and effective tick and mosquito control technologies. This framework shall consider sterilization techniques, safe genetic modification, and use of safe, beneficial bacteria, in alignment with Executive Order 14292 of May 5, 2025 (Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research); and (ii) prioritize and expeditiously advance or register novel tick and mosquito control methods or products that the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency finds to be both safe and effective. (c) Within 90 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, building on the Lyme Disease Moonshot initiative already underway, as appropriate, shall: (i) issue prize competition announcements under 15 U.S.C. 3719 or other applicable laws, or direct research and development programs for rapid diagnostics to identify, prophylactics to prevent — and therapeutics to treat — tick- and mosquito-borne diseases of consequence as determined by the head of the agency, including those listed in subsection 2(b) of this order; and (ii) review available and candidate immunotherapy treatments for alpha-gal syndrome and develop a research agenda to accelerate the clinical review of viable candidates. (d) Within 90 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of Agriculture, in coordination with the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, shall issue prize competition announcements under 15 U.S.C. 3719 or other applicable laws, or direct research programs, for the development of non-chemical means to reduce tick- and mosquito‑borne diseases of consequence, including through reducing tick and mosquito populations. (e) Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Secretary of Agriculture and the Secretary of Health and Human Services, as appropriate, shall explore options for labeling food and drug products that include significant amounts of alpha-galactose, in a manner similar to other allergy warnings. (f) The Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, and the heads of other relevant agencies, in coordination with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall review available resources to support the implementation of this order. Sec . 4 . General Provisions . (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. (b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. (c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person. (d) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of the Interior. DONALD J. TRUMP THE WHITE HOUSE, September 29, 2026. eo-14433 Download

title: Mined, Melted, and Poured in America: President Trump Reverses Years of Anti-Mining Policy
text: Releases Mined, Melted, and Poured in America: President Trump Reverses Years of Anti-Mining Policy The White House September 28, 2026 Today, President Donald J. Trump announced one of the largest steel plants in American history: a $15 billion Mesabi Metallics mill in Iowa. The project will create 1,750 permanent Iowa jobs, support up to 6,000 construction jobs, and is projected to add $95 billion to the U.S. economy over the next decade. The mill will produce 7.5 million tons of steel per year in its first phase, rising to about ten million tons, using iron ore from Mesabi Metallics’ newly opened Minnesota mine — the first new iron ore mine in the United States in 50 years. This is the kind of project Democrats spent years making impossible. The Obama Administration blocked a proposed northern Minnesota copper-nickel mine by denying its federal lease renewals in 2016. The Biden Administration canceled those same leases in 2022, then banned mining for 20 years across 225,504 acres of the Superior National Forest. It revoked a key federal water permit for another long-stalled copper-nickel mine. It blocked a 211-mile road in Alaska that would’ve opened a major copper and cobalt district. In 2024, it piled new rules onto taconite iron-ore processing and coke ovens — the plants that feed American steel — while tariff loopholes kept foreign steel flowing in. President Trump reversed those policies — and American mining is roaring ahead. In 2025, the U.S. surpassed Japan in crude steel production for the first time since 1999 and became the world’s third-largest steel producer. In fact, raw steel output is up 9% since President Trump returned to office. Nearly 6,000 steelworker jobs have been added after almost 10,000 were lost under the prior Administration. American mills now supply 84% of the U.S. finished steel market, up from 77% in 2024. Steel imports are falling as tariffs, permitting reforms, and energy dominance bring production home. New mill orders hit a record $17.3 billion in July 2026; domestic shipments hit a record $16.9 billion that same month. U.S. manufacturing has expanded for eight straight months.

title: Presidential Public Service Announcements Are Nothing New
text: Releases Presidential Public Service Announcements Are Nothing New The White House September 25, 2026 The attacks on President Donald J. Trump’s public service announcements are highly dishonest. The announcements are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action. Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad. That’s not partisanship — that’s a government that still believes in the country it serves. Administrations of both parties have used public service announcements to explain policy and make the case for the nation’s direction: The G.W. Bush Administration ran a national television campaign explaining the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act to seniors. It also bought Super Bowl airtime for anti-drug and anti-terrorism public service announcements . The Obama Administration used national advertising to promote Obamacare subsidies and open enrollment , and a digital campaign to sell its Waters of the United States rule. The Biden Administration poured hundreds of millions of dollars into “ We Can Do This ” — television, digital, radio, and print spots — to drive a nationwide public health message. It’s not just modern Administrations. President Woodrow Wilson’s Committee on Public Information used posters, films, and speakers to rally the country. President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s Office of War Information produced films, radio, and posters to promote the war effort. When prior Administrations utilized the airwaves, it was called “public education.” When this Administration promotes pride in our country, many of those same voices call it “propaganda.” Patriotism isn’t partisan. These public service announcements are unapologetically American, clearly disclosed, and aimed at the country — not a line on the ballot.

title: President Trump, First Lady Conclude Historic China State Visit
text: Releases President Trump, First Lady Conclude Historic China State Visit The White House September 25, 2026 Today, President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump concluded a historic state visit with His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan. This marked the first visit to the White House by a Chinese President in more than a decade — and the first time a Chinese leader has made two formal state visits to the United States. As President Trump said , “The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A… Much has been, and will be, accomplished.” President Trump and the First Lady welcomed President Xi and Madame Peng with an official state arrival ceremony: “President Xi, Madame Peng, and the members of the Chinese delegation, I am delighted to welcome you to the beautiful White House.” President Trump and the First Lady hosted a full official state welcome, including a gift exchange, Silent Drill Platoon review , military review , and flyover — a commanding display of American strength and hospitality. President Trump and President Xi held productive bilateral discussions : “I think our farmers are going to be very happy — a lot of very positive things happened… Great things for both countries. It’s just been very, very productive.” President Trump presented President Xi and Madame Peng with a custom-made statue of a bald eagle at the state dinner: “The bald eagle is a national symbol of the United States and an embodiment of the free and soaring spirit of America — and we hope it will find a nice place, a wonderful place, in Beijing.” President Trump toasted President Xi and Madame Peng at the state dinner: “May all of our people know a future of harmony, peace, and success.” President Trump gave President Xi an exclusive tour of Marine One and the new South Lawn helipad: “He likes granite. He’s an expert on stone, aside from many other things, and he loves good granite.” President Trump and the First Lady hosted tea for President Xi and Madame Peng: “We’ve had a tremendous visit from two spectacular people, and we really enjoyed it — and I think we’ve made tremendous strides. We’ve made great strides. Very positive for both countries.” President Trump and the First Lady hosted President Xi and Madame Peng at the National Archives in recognition of the 250th anniversary of American independence. This state visit showcased the strength of the United States, advanced American economic interests, and made one thing unmistakable: peace and prosperity are strongest when America leads from a position of power.

title: White House Celebrates Recovery Month with a Call to Action for More Recovery Friendly Workplaces
text: Releases White House Celebrates Recovery Month with a Call to Action for More Recovery Friendly Workplaces The White House September 24, 2026 Ceremony Highlights the Trump Administration’s Support for Individuals in Recovery From Drug Addiction and Issues a Call to Action for Recovery Friendly Workplace Policies to Transform our National Workforce Washington, DC – Today, the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy (ONDCP) hosted an event to celebrate National Recovery Month by recognizing recovery friendly workplace policies that support Americans recovering from addiction. Increasing the number of recovery friendly workplaces across the nation is a priority of President Trump’s National Drug Control Strategy , so that the 23 million Americans in treatment and recovery can find support in their employment. The Trump Administration has taken a number of actions reaffirming its commitment to supporting individuals in recovery and helping them reintegrate with their families, communities, and workplaces. Adopting recovery friendly workplace policies strengthens the economy and benefits employers by increasing productivity, and reducing both turnover and health care costs. The ceremony was presided over by ONDCP Director Sara Carter and included remarks by Keith Sonderling, Acting Secretary of Labor; John Figueroa, Acting Under Secretary for Health at the Department of Veterans Affairs; Alice Johnson, White House Pardon Czar; Lynne Patton, Deputy Assistant to President Trump; Kathryn Burgum, White House Senior Advisor for Addiction Recovery; Dr. Timothy Westlake, Chief of Staff of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration; and Steve Messah, Director of the Center for Faith at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. This event featured testimonies by individuals with lived experience of recovery in the workplace, recovery friendly workplace leaders, and employers who shared their experiences implementing recovery friendly workplace policies across the nation. “Recovery friendly workplaces encourage those in recovery to courageously lead healthy and fulfilling lives,” said ONDCP Director Sara Carter. “This National Recovery Month, the Trump Administration renews its commitment to the more than 23 million Americans in recovery. By creating more economic opportunities for Americans in recovery to rebuild their lives after addiction, we help nurture the single most valuable resource in recovery—hope.” “Thanks to President Trump’s economic agenda, trillions of dollars in new investment are flowing into our country and more Americans are working than ever before,” said Acting Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling. “To unleash our full economic potential, we need to connect employers with Americans who are ready to work and that includes millions of Americans in recovery. Through the Great American Recovery Initiative this Administration sees these men and women not only as Americans on the road to recovery, but as valued workers who can contribute to the economy President Trump is revitalizing.” “As a formerly incarcerated woman, I’ve seen people overcome addiction on the inside only to get locked out of opportunity on the outside,” said White House Pardon Czar Alice Johnson. “Recovery takes courage. Second chances take opportunity. Employers across America are already opening doors – and now is the time to open them wider, tap into overlooked talent, and help more people turn recovery into a life of purpose, possibility, and contribution.” “As Executive Director of the Eric Trump Foundation and Vice President at the Trump Organization in 2013, the Trump family held an emotional intervention for me when I relapsed for cocaine addiction. It single-handedly saved my life,” said Lynne Patton, Deputy Assistant to the President. “Every American employee deserves the same unwavering support by their employer and your zip code or resume should not dictate that in 2026.”

title: President Trump at the United Nations: “While Others Have Talked, I Have Acted”

title: President Trump Inks Historic Arctic Security Agreement
text: Releases President Trump Inks Historic Arctic Security Agreement The White House September 22, 2026 Today, President Donald J. Trump joined leaders of Denmark and Greenland to sign an unprecedented agreement giving the United States lasting control over security interests in Greenland. The landmark agreement — which comes at no cost to American taxpayers — forever guarantees America the ability to defend the continent, includes permanent basing rights, and bars any U.S. adversary from establishing a base, military presence, or sensitive investment without America’s approval. The agreement is being hailed at home and around the world as a decisive victory for American security and a stronger NATO in the Arctic. Here’s what they’re saying: President Donald J. Trump : “As I announced just days ago, the U.S. has also reached an unprecedented agreement regarding the Northern Frontier of North America — the large and strategically vital piece of land known as Greenland. This agreement… gives the United States permanent control over security and all other needs on that territory. We will have the complete ability to do what is necessary to defend the American continent.” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen : “This day represents a milestone in our longstanding cooperation. 75 years ago, we entered into an agreement about the defense of Greenland. Today, we are signing an even bigger and better agreement — a deal that can last forever. This deal is good for the United States, it’s good for Greenland, for Denmark, for the NATO alliance, and therefore, also good for Europe. In other words, we are strengthening our common security, boosting our common deterrence, showing our adversaries who we are — and we are doing it together.” Prime Minister of Greenland Jens-Frederik Nielsen : “We are, have been, and will remain a steadfast friend of the United States and a part of the Western alliance. Your security is our security and our security is your security. We are truly pleased with the result that strengthens our shared security and strengthens our bond as close allies. This agreement is historical.” Danish Minister for Foreign Affairs Lars Løkke Rasmussen : “An important moment today. Greenland, Denmark and the United States have signed an agreement strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. It’s been a bumpy ride. But here we are – with a deal in hand that we can all be very satisfied with. We share a long history. And we share a responsibility for the security of our region. Today, we take another important step together – with full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Greenlandic people’s right to self-determination. History binds us together. Our future demands that we stand together.” NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte : “Great to see the deal signed by the United States, Denmark, and Greenland today. We know the threats we face, and greater security in the Arctic and North Atlantic is essential for Europe and North America alike. This agreement, along with NATO’s growing role in securing this vital region, enhances our collective security and supports a safer and more stable future for us all” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen : “I welcome today’s agreement on strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic. My visit to Greenland earlier this month underscored the strategic importance of the region and the scale of the challenges. Challenges we will face together. As always, the EU will work closely with Denmark and Greenland and our international partners.” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz : “Good news for the security of Greenland: The agreement between Denmark, Greenland, and the USA strengthens our partnership in NATO and security in the High North. title: G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Concludes with Four Consensus Outcomes
text: Releases G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Concludes with Four Consensus Outcomes The White House September 21, 2026 On Wednesday, September 16 th , 2026, G20 Energy Ministers concluded the Energy Abundance Ministerial in Houston, Texas. The Ministerial was hosted by the White House National Energy Dominance Council (NEDC), the Department of the Interior, the Department of Energy, and the Environmental Protection Agency. At the conclusion of the Ministerial, G20 Ministers reached consensus on four outcomes advancing energy access, infrastructure development, water resilience, and supply chain security. The outcomes advance the Energy Abundance Working Group’s three pillars: Energy Security and Affordable Baseload, Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency, and Critical Minerals and Resilient Supply Chains. Together, they support the common sense solutions that President Trump has championed to increase energy availability, speed the development of critical infrastructure, strengthen water resilience, and reduce vulnerabilities in the supply chains essential to modern economies. Ministers reached consensus on deliverables that support affordable, scalable, and context-specific pathways to expand household energy access, including the use of liquefied petroleum gas, or LPG , where it is a reliable and scalable means of rapidly displacing traditional biomass. They also reached agreement on Permitting and Regulatory Efficiency to encourage more efficient, predictable, and effective domestic permitting and regulatory processes, and a Water Reuse Initiative outlining voluntary, fit-for-purpose water reuse to strengthen resilience for communities, energy production, manufacturing, agriculture, and other critical sectors. Finally, Ministers agreed in the Critical Minerals Statement on voluntary cooperation to build resilient, affordable, secure, and diversified critical minerals value chains through information sharing, innovation, investment, capacity building, and local value addition. “The world cannot build secure energy systems, advanced manufacturing capacity, or digital infrastructure on fragile mineral supply chains,” said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, Chair of the National Energy Dominance Council. “The consensus reached in Houston supports a common sense approach: diversify supply, strengthen domestic and regional capacity, encourage investment and innovation, and respect each nation’s sovereignty over its natural resources. These steps will help reduce overreliance on any single supplier while creating more durable supply chains and greater economic opportunity.” “Energy is the essential ingredient that enables everything we do,” said Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “A highly energized society brings health, wealth, and opportunity. The consensus reached in Houston advances cooperation to expand the affordable, reliable, and secure energy, infrastructure, and supply chains needed to support prosperity, resilience, and opportunity throughout the world.” “President Trump’s energy abundance agenda reflects reality – strong environmental stewardship and economic prosperity go hand in hand,” said Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin. “The consensus reached in Houston advances solutions that streamline processes without sacrificing safeguards, expand water resilience, and enable the infrastructure needed to deliver reliable and affordable energy. This is how the G20 can support growth, protect communities, and meet the demands of the future.” The investments and agreements announced in Houston demonstrate how President Trump’s energy abundance agenda is creating jobs, delivering economic opportunity, strengthening American manufacturing, and expanding the energy infrastructure needed to power the future. The Japanese company Hitachi Energy announced a $528 million investment to build a new power transformer manufacturing facility in Gallman, Mississippi, expected to create 654 new jobs. Houston-based Caturus announced a five-train expansion of its Commonwealth LNG export facility in Louisiana that would add 7.75 million tonnes per annum of capacity and nearly double the project’s planned capacity to approximately 17.25 million tonnes per annum, Continental Resources signed a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela’s PDVSA to develop and operate the 126,000-acre Ayacucho 2 Block in the Orinoco Belt, which Continental estimates contains approximately 30 billion barrels of oil. At the Ministerial, Administrator Zeldin announced the EPA’s repeal of the majority of the Biden Administration’s greenhouse gas requirements for U.S. power plants, the largest power sector deregulatory action in American history. EPA projects the repeal will save $310 billion and help unleash America’s vast energy resources, including coal and natural gas. The Administrator also proposed to repeal the remaining power sector standards, which would save an additional $370 million in direct compliance costs. Together, these actions will restore reliable, affordable baseload power and strengthen American energy dominance. Representatives from the following nations and unions were present at the three-day Ministerial: the African Union, the Argentine Republic, the Commonwealth of Australia, the Federative Republic of Brazil, Canada, the People’s Republic of China, the European Union, the French Republic, the Federal Republic of Germany, the Republic of India, the Republic of Indonesia, the Italian Republic, Japan, the United Mexican States, the Republic of Poland, the Russian Federation, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Republic of Korea, the Republic of Türkiye, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

title: White House Access Is a Privilege — Not a Right
text: Releases White House Access Is a Privilege — Not a Right The White House September 21, 2026 Last week, President Donald J. Trump removed CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House grounds after years of false reporting . The First Amendment protects their right to publish; it does not entitle them to a hard pass, briefing room seat, or place in the press pool. Access changes are nothing new. What is new, however, is the sudden claim that it becomes sacred only when the outlets are friendly to the Radical Left. The rule was never “every outlet gets in.” It was always “our side stays in.” For years, Democrat Administrations have restricted, punished, and locked out the press. 2009: The Obama White House branded Fox News as the “research arm” and “communications arm” of the Republican Party, barred it from a round of exclusive Sunday show interviews, instructed agencies to “skip” including it in pooled coverage, derided it as “really not news,” and undertook an all-out effort to isolate the organization. Barack Hussein Obama now calls a Fox ban “unimaginable,” but his White House tried it — and his spokesman admitted they were willing to do it. 2010: The Obama Justice Department labeled Fox News correspondent James Rosen a possible “co-conspirator” in a criminal leak case, secretly monitored his emails and phone calls, and tracked his movements — an “unprecedented” level of surveillance and intimidation of a journalist over his reporting. 2011: Obama White House officials restricted the Boston Herald from coverage — writing that pool slots depended on covering Obama “fairly” — after the paper ran a front page Mitt Romney op-ed. 2011: After a San Francisco Chronicle reporter recorded protesters interrupting an Obama fundraiser, White House officials threatened to strip the outlet from access and warned of retaliation if the paper reported on it. 2012: The Obama Justice Department secretly seized two months of telephone records covering more than 20 Associated Press lines used by more than a dozen journalists — targeting them over their reporting. 2023: The Biden White House blocked New York Post reporter Steven Nelson from covering the President’s only daytime public event — despite empty seats in the room — after the reporter pressed Biden on his family’s shady business dealings. 2023: The Biden Administration restricted more than 440 reporters from White House access through a new, retroactive press credentialing process — with independent and conservative journalists taking a heavy share of the hit. The White House Correspondents’ Association barely objected. 2008: In the Obama campaign’s final days, senior campaign officials pulled reporters from three prominent outlets off the traveling press plane — restricting them from coverage after the papers endorsed Obama’s opponent. 2021: The same media now suing once urged a ban on Fox News. CNN’s Brian Stelter repeatedly floated removing Fox News from the White House press tool as a “political tool,” and later even suggested Fox News be dropped from cable altogether. During the first 100 days of President Trump’s second term, the Media Research Center found that 92% of coverage by mainstream outlets was negative compared to nearly 60% positive coverage during the same period under Biden. That’s more like a political operation with cameras than a free press holding power to account. No President is required to host a hostile operation on the grounds. Access has always been a privilege — and President Trump is applying that rule.

title: WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Historic Victories for America’s Hunters, Anglers, and Outdoorsmen
text: Releases WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Historic Victories for America’s Hunters, Anglers, and Outdoorsmen The White House September 18, 2026 President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promises to America’s outdoorsmen by cutting red tape, removing burdensome and unnecessary restrictions levied by previous Administrations and expanding America’s great outdoor recreation sector that generates over $1.2 trillion annually and supports over 5 million jobs. Last night, the President signed two Executive Orders to bolster American hunting and revive American saltwater angling. Industry leaders and stakeholders nationwide hailed the President’s leadership and commitment to restoring Americans’ access to Federal lands, revitalizing our Nation’s outdoor recreation economy, while conserving and protecting America’s abundant natural resources. Here’s what they are saying: Secretary Doug Burgum: “Sportsmen are among our greatest conservationists, and this administration is committed to supporting the men and women who help protect our public lands and wildlife. At @POTUS’ direction, @Interior will: Expand hunting access Promote habitat management Improve migratory bird hunting authorizations Encourage Sunday hunting Support hunter education and youth and veteran programs Putting American hunters, fishermen and outdoorsmen FIRST.” Senator Tom Cotton: “Hunting is an important part of Arkansas’s culture and economy. Thankful President Trump is prioritizing America’s hunting heritage for future generations.” Rep. Bruce Westerman: “Today’s executive orders signed by President Trump are generational victories for America’s sportsmen and women. The actions taken by President Trump expand access to public lands and waters, eliminate burdensome regulation, reinvigorate our outdoor economy and invest in the next generation of hunters and anglers. I’m proud to have advanced legislation on many of these policies through the Natural Resources Committee, including the reauthorization of the Great American Outdoors Act. I look forward to working with the Trump administration to codify these executive orders and support our nation’s hunters and anglers.” Rep. August Pfluger: “For years, Washington made it harder to access the public lands and waters that belong to the American people. Today’s executive order by @POTUS expands wildlife access to hunters and anglers, rolls back overreaching Biden-era restrictions like the lead ammunition mandates, and opens up more opportunities for the next generation of sportsmen. I’m proud to support this action and applaud President Trump for rolling back the overreach of the previous administration.” Rep. Addison McDowell: “Proud to join hundreds of anglers and hunters tonight as President Trump just signed an executive order reversing Biden-era restrictions on America’s outdoorsmen. By cutting burdensome red tape on fishermen and bringing outdoor recreation into the 21st century, President Trump is putting the American Outdoorsman First!” The National Rifle Association : “The NRA is proud to stand beside @POTUS to protect the Second Amendment nationwide. We applaud President Trump’s newest executive orders protecting the storied tradition of American outdoorsmanship. 🤝” Center for Sportfish Policy President and CEO Jeff Angers: “This Executive Order is a historic recognition of what millions of American anglers and coastal communities have known for decades: marine recreational fishing deserves a management system built for the way Americans fish. By prioritizing better data, stronger state partnerships and modern management approaches, President Trump’s order builds on our conservation gains creating a path to more reliable access and opportunity in America’s oceans.” National Shooting Sports Foundation President and CEO Joe Bartozzi : “Today’s Executive Order by President Trump demonstrates that this administration stands with America’s sportsmen and women. This is a tremendous victory to ensure that America’s hunting heritage is protected for today’s hunters and the coming generations of outdoorsmen and women. NSSF has long championed several of these key policy issues, including protecting the right to use traditional ammunition, accessing public lands and increasing opportunities for Sunday hunting. We are proud to have led this fight and prouder still that the Trump administration is embracing commonsense policies to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports across America.” Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation President and CEO Jeff Crane : “The Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation commends President Trump for bringing together leaders from across the sportsmen’s community and recognizing the tremendous contributions hunters, anglers, trappers, and recreational shooters make to our nation. America’s outdoor heritage is one of our nation’s greatest traditions, and today’s event demonstrates the President’s continued commitment to ensuring these traditions remain strong for generations to come.” Ducks Unlimited CEO Adam Putnam : “Hunters have been our nation’s most ardent conservationists for generations, and it’s terrific to see President Trump publicly recognize that in the White House Rose Garden. This Executive Order is an acknowledgment of hunters’ longstanding contributions to conservation, hunting access, sound waterfowl science, and hunter education. Our proud hunting heritage has been woven into the fabric of our great nation’s identity for 250 years, and this sort of commitment will help ensure it remains that way for future generations.” Delta Waterfowl CEO Jason Tharpe : “We sincerely appreciate the President’s Executive Order as it highlights a number of Delta’s priorities for both ducks and duck hunters. Having the President affirm the need for access, addressing infrastructure on public lands, enhancing habitat through agreements with willing landowners and ensuring waterfowl hunting regulations are based on the best available data are all core needs and we appreciate the President’s leadership. Delta Waterfowl is deeply appreciative of President Trump’s historic announcement in furtherance of America’s hunting and conservation heritage. Simply put, this executive order will serve to benefit ducks and duck hunters for years to come and we look forward to working closely with the administration toward its implementation.” National Marine Manufacturers Association President and CEO Frank Hugelmeyer : “Recreational boating and fishing are the foundation of America’s outdoor heritage and an important driver of our nation’s recreation economy. Thank you to President Trump and his administration for recognizing the value of outdoor recreation and the American industries and communities it supports.” Coastal Conservation Association President and CEO Pat Murray : “We’re grateful the Administration has taken this opportunity to emphasize the social and economic importance of recreational fishing. State-based management has never been more important for our federal fisheries and we applaud this critical need being highlighted in this Executive Order.” American Sportfishing Association President and CEO Glenn Hughes : “The American Sportfishing Association thanks President Trump for this decisive action to improve management and data collection for America’s saltwater fisheries. This Executive Order will have long-term benefits for the sportfishing industry and America’s 15.5 million saltwater recreational anglers.” Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation President and CEO Kyle Weaver: “On behalf of the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation (RMEF), we thank President Trump and his administration for recognizing the vital role hunters play in sustaining wildlife and for issuing the Reinvigorating America’s Hunting Heritage Executive Order that strongly aligns with RMEF’s mission to ensure the future of elk, other wildlife, their habitat and our hunting heritage. We are particularly excited about the effort to expand wild game donation programs across the United States and our members, the small meat processors of the country who butcher the vast majority of the wild game meat, stand ready to help keep this promise to the American people.” National Deer Association President and CEO Nick Pinizzotto: “The National Deer Association is proud to celebrate the announcement of a Hunter’s Bill of Rights, especially the President’s keen attention to the issue of venison donation. title: RESTRICTION ON ENTRY OF CERTAIN NONIMMIGRANT WORKERS
text: Presidential Actions RESTRICTION ON ENTRY OF CERTAIN NONIMMIGRANT WORKERS Proclamations September 18, 2026 BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA A PROCLAMATION On September 19, 2025, Proclamation 10973 (Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers) (2025 Proclamation), was issued to address significant abuses of the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program. The restrictions enacted by the 2025 Proclamation have proven to be highly effective but the underlying conditions necessitating the restrictions persist. It is therefore in the interests of the United States to extend the 2025 Proclamation for an additional 12 months, until 12:00 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 21, 2027. As explained in the 2025 Proclamation, the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program was created to bring temporary workers in high-skilled functions into the United States, but it has been exploited to replace, not supplement, American workers with lower-paid labor. Certain employers, including information technology (IT) staffing and outsourcing firms, have abused the system to suppress wages and displace American workers, and this has both harmed the labor market for American workers while also making it difficult to attract and retain the most highly skilled temporary workers. IT staffing and outsourcing firms were found to supply a large volume of entry-level temporary H‑1B workers, generally at a much lower salary compared to full‑time, traditional workers, and some of these firms later outsourced IT roles to cheap labor markets overseas. This has led to a proliferation of lower-paid foreign labor flooding the American labor market and making it difficult for American workers and recent graduates, especially in science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields, to find employment. To combat these abuses, the 2025 Proclamation set forth a restriction on entry of certain H-1B nonimmigrant workers, except for those petitions that were accompanied or supplemented by a $100,000 payment, subject to very limited exceptions. The 2025 Proclamation went into effect on September 21, 2025, and, since then, the $100,000 payment has been made for over 700 petitions. Additionally, the 2025 Proclamation required initiation of rulemakings by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Department of Labor (DOL) to address systemic H-1B program concerns. On December 29, 2025, DHS published a final rule, titled Weighted Selection Process for Registrants and Petitioners Seeking to File Cap-Subject H-1B Petitions, 90 Fed. Reg. 60864 (DHS final rule), to address the policy goals consistent with section 4(b) of the 2025 Proclamation. Through this rule, DHS created and implemented a weighted selection process that prioritizes the allocation of visas to higher-skilled and higher-paid aliens to better protect the wages, working conditions, and job opportunities for American workers. This policy better serves the intent of the H-1B statutory scheme, incentivizes employers to recruit temporary workers for roles at the highest pay and skill levels, and was in effect for the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 H-1B cap season. On March 27, 2026, DOL published a notice of proposed rulemaking, titled Improving Wage Protections for the Temporary and Permanent Employment of Certain Foreign Nationals in the United States, 91 Fed. Reg. 15454, to address the policy goals consistent with section 4(a) of the 2025 Proclamation. The DOL’s analysis of labor condition application data found that the average wage actually paid to H-1B workers, and the prevailing wage assigned to their positions, both remain well below the average wage earned by comparable American workers. The rule, once finalized, will better align prevailing wage levels with wages paid to similarly employed and located American workers and will strengthen overall program integrity. Finally, my Administration continues to explore other complementary efforts that would, among other things, reform the H-1B program and assist with cost-recovery for immigration program administration. Since the effective date of the 2025 Proclamation and subsequent promulgation of the DHS final rule, there have been several measurable impacts on the H-1B program, including a significant reduction in H-1B registrations filed by large IT outsourcing firms, with the largest IT staffing and outsourcing firms reducing their combined H-1B registrations from 24,946 to 2,055, a 92 percent decrease. There has also been a large reduction in consular processing requests, which are used to bring workers into the United States, noting a nearly 97 percent decrease from the FY 2025 to FY 2027 cap seasons. Finally, there has been a positive shift in FY 2027 H-1B registration and selection data toward higher-skilled and higher-paid workers, with registrations for beneficiaries with at least a U.S. Master’s degree rising from 45.1 percent of total registrants for FY 2026 to 66.1 percent for FY 2027. Job offers with wages corresponding to the two highest wage levels accounted for approximately 46.3 percent of H-1B registration selections while those corresponding with the lowest wage level accounted for only 17.8 percent. It is reasonable to conclude that the required $100,000 payment and newly implemented weighted selection process have had the combined effect of deterring low-wage and low-skilled recruitment while increasing access for high-skilled and high-wage workers, as intended by the 2025 Proclamation. Although the 2025 Proclamation and subsequent rulemaking have had the desired effects, the underlying conditions precipitating their issuance persist and, without an extension of the 2025 Proclamation, it is highly likely that progress will halt and program abuse will resume, undermining American workers and posing a threat to the labor market that would be detrimental to the interests of the United States. The 2025 Proclamation highlighted a number of concerns, including high unemployment rates for recent graduates, wage suppression, fraud, and national security threats. Currently, these issues continue to undermine our economy, with unemployment rates for recent college graduates standing at 5.7 percent as of June 2026, a marginal decrease from September 2025, when the rate was 5.8 percent. Underemployment for recent college graduates also continues to cause concern, having risen from 41.8 percent in September 2025 to 42 percent as of June 2026. Additionally, while DOL is actively in the process of promulgating a rule to restore integrity to the prevailing wage system, it will take a significant amount of time to correct and balance the labor market. Finally, while fraud and abuse continue to be identified and investigated, these are ongoing and pervasive concerns that require a sustained, comprehensive response reflected in the entry restriction imposed by the 2025 Proclamation. A review of the 2025 Proclamation’s impacts and other recent policy changes has shown significant measurable changes in H-1B filing patterns that demonstrate the effectiveness of the 2025 Proclamation and a need for its extension. An extension of the 2025 Proclamation will continue to protect the economic and national security interests of the United States, improve labor market access for American workers and graduates, and ensure that employers recruit only the most highly-skilled and essential alien workers when needed in line with the original intent of the program. As a result, the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretary of Homeland Security have jointly recommended an extension of the 2025 Proclamation. As a result of these reviews and considerations, I have decided to continue to impose the limitations set forth in Proclamation 10973 on the entry into the United States by certain nonimmigrant workers. Accordingly, by the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, it is hereby ordered: Section 1 . Restriction on Entry . (a) Pursuant to sections 212(f) and 215(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) (8 U.S.C. 1182(f) and 1185(a)), the entry into the United States of aliens as nonimmigrants to perform services in a specialty occupation under section 101(a)(15)(H)(i)(b) of the INA (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)(H)(i)(b)), is restricted, except for those aliens whose petitions are accompanied or supplemented by a payment of $100,000 — subject to the exceptions set forth in subsection (c) of this section. This restriction shall expire, absent extension, 12 months after the effective date of this proclamation, which shall be 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 21, 2026. (b) The Secretary of Homeland Security shall restrict decisions on petitions not accompanied by a $100,000 payment for H-1B specialty occupation workers under section 101(a)(15)(H)(i)(b) of the INA, who are currently outside the United States, for 12 months following the effective date of this proclamation as set forth in subsection (a) of this section. (c) The restriction imposed pursuant to subsections (a) and (b) of this section shall not apply to any individual alien, all aliens working for a company, or all aliens working in an industry, if the Secretary of Homeland Security determines, in the Secretary’s discretion, that the hiring of such aliens to be employed as H-1B specialty occupation workers is in the national interest and does not pose a threat to the security or welfare of the United States. Sec . 2 . Compliance . (a) Employers shall, prior to filing an H-1B petition on behalf of an alien outside the United States, obtain and retain documentation showing that the payment described in section 1 of this proclamation has been made. (b) The Secretary of State shall verify receipt of payment of the amount described in section 1 of this proclamation during the H-1B visa petition process and shall approve only those visa applications for which the filing employer has made the payment described in section 1 of this proclamation. (c) The Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security shall coordinate to take all necessary and appropriate action to implement this proclamation and to deny entry to the United States to any H-1B nonimmigrant for whom the prospective employer has not made the payment described in section 1 of this proclamation. Sec . 3 . Scope and Implementation of Restriction on Entry . (a) The restriction on entry pursuant to section 1 of this proclamation shall apply only to aliens who enter or attempt to enter the United States after the effective date of this proclamation as set forth in section 1(a) of this proclamation. This restriction applies to aliens who must seek admission to the United States to effectuate the approval of a petition described in section 1 of this proclamation, including through consular notification, notification at a port of entry, pre‑flight inspection, or pre-clearance.
